title: Normalized reconstruction and transported adjunction transposes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. On a fixed small skeleton of its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $B_{n,W}=(R/\varpi^n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\varprojlim_n B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear $B_{n,W}$-module systems, with componentwise morphisms, of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and use its unbounded derived category. Write $\mathscr N_W$ for the full subcategory with all transition adjoints $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,W}}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ invertible for $m\ge n$, and $\mathscr C_W\subset D(\widehat R_W)$ for the full subcategory of derived-complete complexes [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-derived-complete]. No cohomological bound, constructibility, uniform Tor interval or equipped local model is assumed.

Let $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ be the specified reduction/total-limit adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with unit $u$ and counit $e$; thus $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ U_W$, where $U_W$ restricts each coefficient sheaf to $\widehat R_W$. It restricts to an adjoint equivalence $\mathscr C_W\rightleftarrows\mathscr N_W$. Its actual unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ and actual counit $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$ are natural isomorphisms on these subcategories. In particular the coefficient comparisons are the scalar-extension adjoints of the specified total-limit projections.

For schemes $X,Y$ with these same coefficient data, suppose $F:\mathscr N_X\rightleftarrows\mathscr N_Y:G$ is an adjunction with counit $\epsilon$. Then $\bar F=\mathcal L_YF\mathcal R_X$ is left adjoint to $\bar G=\mathcal L_XG\mathcal R_Y$, with counit at $K\in\mathscr C_Y$ equal to
$$\bar\epsilon_K=u_K^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_Y(\epsilon_{\mathcal R_YK})\circ\mathcal L_YF(e_{G\mathcal R_YK}).$$
For any $N\in\mathscr N_Y$ and system map $a:P\to GN$, $P\in\mathscr N_X$, put $\bar a=\mathcal L_X(a)$. Under the natural identifications $\bar F\mathcal L_XP\cong\mathcal L_YFP$ and $\bar G\mathcal L_YN\cong\mathcal L_XGN$ induced by $e$, its adjoint transpose is exactly $\mathcal L_Y(\epsilon_N\circ F(a))$. These identifications are natural for system maps. For composable system functors $F:\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$ and $H:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_Z$, the comparison between $\bar H\bar F$ and $\mathcal L_ZHF\mathcal R_X$ is $\mathcal L_ZH(e_{F\mathcal R_X(-)})$, with the corresponding naturality for transformations. More generally, all these assertions hold with $\mathscr N_X,\mathscr N_Y,\mathscr N_Z$ replaced by full subcategories $\mathscr N'_W\subset\mathscr N_W$ closed under isomorphism, $\mathscr C_W$ replaced by the full subcategory $\mathscr C'_W$ of those $K\in\mathscr C_W$ with $\mathcal R_WK\in\mathscr N'_W$, and $F,G,H$ functors (resp. an adjunction $F\dashv G$) defined only between these subcategories; $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ restricts to an adjoint equivalence $\mathscr C'_W\rightleftarrows\mathscr N'_W$ since $\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\cong N$.

proof.text: For each scheme W, use the specified reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. On a flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ of an ambient complex, the component of $\mathcal R_W$ is $Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_{n,W}$; associativity of scalar extension identifies its further reduction from level $m$ to level $n$ with $Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_{n,W}$. Thus $\mathcal R_W$ lands in $\mathscr N_W$, and its unit and counit are the specified maps of the evaluation-calculus statement.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, reduction/total-limit adjunction and normalized coefficient systems

proof.text: If $N\in\mathscr N_W$, [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] gives that $\mathcal L_WN$ is derived complete and that each canonical reduction $(\mathcal L_WN)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ is an isomorphism. The evaluation-calculus counit $e_N$ has exactly these scalar-extension adjoints as its components, so all derived evaluations of $e_N$ are isomorphisms. Since evaluations detect isomorphisms in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, effectivity and counit reconstruction

proof.text: For derived-complete $K$, the adjunction triangle gives $e_{\mathcal R_WK}\circ\mathcal R_W(u_K)=1_{\mathcal R_WK}$. The counit is invertible by the preceding step, hence $\mathcal R_W(u_K)$ is invertible. Its component at $n=1$ is the first derived reduction of the actual unit $u_K$, by the unit normalization in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The source $K$ is derived complete by hypothesis and the target $\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ is derived complete by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]; [sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama] therefore makes $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ an isomorphism.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, derived-complete unit and derived-Nakayama argument

proof.text: The restricted functors $\mathcal R_W:\mathscr C_W\to\mathscr N_W$ and $\mathcal L_W:\mathscr N_W\to\mathscr C_W$ retain the adjunction, and both its unit and counit are natural isomorphisms by the preceding steps. The triangle identities then exhibit these restrictions as mutually inverse equivalences. The same argument applies to any replete full $\mathscr N'_W\subset\mathscr N_W$: define $\mathscr C'_W=\{K\in\mathscr C_W\mid\mathcal R_WK\in\mathscr N'_W\}$; closure under isomorphism and the two natural isomorphisms show that the adjunction restricts to an equivalence on $\mathscr C'_W$ and $\mathscr N'_W$.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, restriction to replete full subcategories

proof.text:
Given $F\dashv G$ with counit $\epsilon$, compose the three adjunction bijections for $\mathcal L_X\dashv\mathcal R_X$, $F\dashv G$, and $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$. This proves $\bar F=\mathcal L_YF\mathcal R_X\dashv\bar G=\mathcal L_XG\mathcal R_Y$. Tracing the identity of $\bar G K$ through these bijections gives the counit at $K$ as
$$\bar\epsilon_K=u_K^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_Y(\epsilon_{\mathcal R_YK})\circ\mathcal L_YF(e_{G\mathcal R_YK}).$$
Here the last comparison is the counit $e$ of $\mathcal R_X\dashv\mathcal L_X$, and the first comparison is the inverse of the unit $u_K$ of $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, counit of the transported adjunction

proof.text: For $a:P\to GN$, transpose $\bar a=\mathcal L_X(a)$ through the transported Hom bijection. Naturality of the counit gives $e_{G N}\circ\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(a)=a\circ e_P$. Substituting this equality into the three Hom bijections cancels the adjacent unit/counit pairs by the triangle identities, leaving precisely $\mathcal L_Y(\epsilon_N\circ F(a))$. Therefore the stated identifications $\bar F\mathcal L_XP\cong\mathcal L_YFP$ and $\bar G\mathcal L_YN\cong\mathcal L_XGN$ carry the transpose of $\bar a$ to that map; naturality follows from naturality of $u,e$ and of $\epsilon$.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, transported transpose and counit naturality

proof.text: For composable $F$ and $H$, expand $\bar H\bar F$ and insert the counit isomorphism $e_{F\mathcal R_X(-)}$ between the middle factors $\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y$. This yields the comparison $\mathcal L_ZH(e_{F\mathcal R_X(-)})$ with $\mathcal L_ZHF\mathcal R_X$. Naturality of $e$ gives the corresponding equality for natural transformations. Restricting all formulas to the replete subcategories $\mathscr N'_W,\mathscr C'_W$ is valid because every displayed functor and transformation preserves those subcategories by their definition.
